newsitem.title: GERMANY: German parliament plans to move to Berlin in 1999.
newsitem.headline: German parliament plans to move to Berlin in 1999.

text.p: The president of Germany's parliament Rita Suessmuth said on Monday it would move from Bonn to the new capital Berlin on schedule in spring 1999.
Speaking to journalists during a tour of the Reichstag building, Suessmuth said the extensive remodelling and renovation of the parliament building in Berlin would be completed on time in late 1998.
"We are staying with our plan to commence our work in Berlin in the spring of 1999," said Suessmuth.
Parliament voted narrowly in 1991 to move the seat of government from Bonn to Berlin, a year after East and West Germany united.

Diehard opponents of the decision, which will cost about 20 billion marks ($12 billion), have succeeded in delaying but not stopping the move. They will mark the sixth anniversary of the vote on June 20 with rallies in Bonn.

Suessmuth said that the parliament would start working in Berlin in early 1999 even though some of the office buildings for parliamentarians being built around the Reichstag would not be finished by then.

"There is a considerable amount of office space that the parliament will be able to use," Suessmuth said. She added that it would not be necessary for every government official to begin their work in Berlin at the same time as deputies.
She said that there was already enough office space available in Berlin for all 673 deputies. She urged opponents of the move not to raise new hurdles.

The remodelling of the Reichstag building, one of the biggest construction sites in Berlin, will cost about 600 million marks ($350 million). The outside walls have been completed and work will soon begin on a 23.5 metre (75 foot) -high glass dome on top of the building. ($ = 1.723 German Marks)
